sources_and_data.use: Dependency: exact at-most-crossing interface, two-sided series/parallel composition, terminal-free scalar closure, and feasible k>=2 path obstruction.
Preserved the Multiway-Cut feasibility gate and separation between contraction-only claims and arbitrary sparsifiers.
Complete mathematical exposition and proof audit for this task.

method.type: direct mathematical derivation with adversarial proof audit; no experiment or network search
method.quantifiers: all finite two-terminal series-parallel multigraphs, all finite unweighted multigraphs for the terminal-free scalar sublemma, finite metrics, injective terminal assignments, and integer crossing budgets
method.interface: I_N(q;a,b,rho): minimum metric-labeling cost with boundary labels, prescribed internal terminal assignment rho, and at most q crossings
checked_directions: terminal-free scalar closure proved by cut lower bound, layer-cake metric lower bound, and matching minimum-cut labeling
terminal-bearing obstruction evaluated exactly from the unique all-terminal path labeling

mathematical_claim: The terminal-free scalar interface is an exact standard metric/min-cut consequence for every finite unweighted multigraph with two distinguished boundaries, not a series-parallel novelty. It does not extend to all terminal-bearing modules under a label-blind state: a feasible two-edge path has exact costs 3 and 4 under two valid metrics with the same endpoint distance, connectivity, endpoint labels, and budget.
assumptions: Graphs are finite undirected unweighted multigraphs; parallel edges are separate edge terms and loops contribute zero.
The interface uses an at-most crossing budget q and is +infinity when no admissible labeling exists.
Boundary labels are prescribed, internal terminal labels are prescribed and injective, and the metric is finite.
The claimed obstruction concerns only states that discard all internal terminal labels and retain endpoint labels, connectivity, and budget; it is not a lower bound for arbitrary sparsifiers.
verified_steps: For terminal-free modules, every unequal-boundary labeling crosses an s-t cut and the metric triangle inequality gives the edgewise lower bound.
The layer-cake identity is the full integral from 0 to infinity; truncation to [0, mu(a,b)] is used only as a lower bound because internal distances can exceed the endpoint distance.
A minimum s-t cut labeling attains lambda times mu(a,b), while equal boundary labels use the constant labeling; this proves both directions of the scalar formula.
The same proof applies to arbitrary finite unweighted multigraphs with no internal terminals; series-parallel structure is only a way to compute lambda.
On the feasible path s-x-t with all vertices terminal and q=k=2, both edges necessarily cross and the unique labeling has cost mu(a,c)+mu(c,b).
The two metrics have mu_1(a,b)=mu_2(a,b)=2 but sums 1+2=3 and 2+2=4, so a label-blind scalar state cannot preserve both exact values.
gaps: No compact metric-aware, label-dependent graph-realizable representation for terminal-bearing series-parallel modules was proved.
The raw interface table has explicit dependence on the internal-terminal labels and is not an output-graph size bound.
No lower bound was proved against arbitrary joint contractions or arbitrary terminal-preserving sparsifiers.

counterexamples.claim_refuted: Endpoint labels, two-terminal connectivity, and crossing budget alone suffice for every terminal-bearing module.
counterexamples.graph: two-edge path s-x-t with all three vertices terminal
counterexamples.metric_2: D={a,b,c}; all three pairwise distances are 2
counterexamples.verification: Both are valid metrics, both have endpoint distance 2, and the exact costs are 3 and 4. The instance is feasible because its terminal Multiway Cut has size 2.

reviewed: The layer-cake truncation direction was corrected.
The scalar lemma was checked without using series-parallel decomposition.
The path witness was checked directly from its unique terminal labeling and two metrics.
The review rejected promotion of a finite table or scalar obstruction to a sparsifier-size theorem.
independent_review.scope: The result is a standard terminal-free interface lemma plus a finite feasible obstruction to one label-blind compression class; the broader sparsifier question remains open.

observed_result_or_blocker.positive_result: Restricted compression lemma proved: for R_N empty, I_N(q;a,b)=0 when a=b; lambda_N*mu(a,b) when a!=b and q>=lambda_N; and +infinity otherwise.

feasible_obstruction.graph: two-edge path s-x-t with all three vertices terminals
feasible_obstruction.independent_check: two terminal edges necessarily cross, and deleting both is a Multiway Cut of size 2
feasible_obstruction.two_metric_witness: mu_1(a,b)=2, mu_1(a,c)=1, mu_1(c,b)=2 gives 3; mu_2(a,b)=2, mu_2(a,c)=2, mu_2(c,b)=2 gives 4, with the same graph, endpoint labels, connectivity, and q=2

observed_result_or_blocker.scope_blocker: The obstruction refutes only label-blind structural compression. A symbolic or metric-aware label-dependent compression, and the unrestricted sparsifier-size question, remain open.

state_size_accounting.raw_table_upper_bound: At most (|E_N|+1)|D|^(|R_N|+2) positions, or (k+1)|D|^(|R_N|+2) when budgets are truncated to k.
state_size_accounting.interpretation: This is a direct finite-table upper bound, not a sparsifier lower bound, representative-set lower bound, or contraction lower bound.
state_size_accounting.dependence: Internal-terminal count |R_N| and label universe |D| are explicit; no hidden exponent-free compression was established.

proved: both directions of the terminal-free cost/crossing characterization
unresolved: general label-dependent compression with no hidden |D|- or s-dependent exponent
any sparsifier-size lower bound for terminal-bearing series-parallel modules

uncertainty: The fixed-metric path witness rules out the stated label-blind state class, not every possible compressed representation.
Raw interface-table cardinality does not establish a sparsifier lower bound.
No conclusion is drawn about Paper 3 outcomes; Target A and Target B remain unchanged.
next_falsifiable_action: Specify a candidate metric-aware label-dependent compressed state and prove both reconstruction directions for series and parallel composition; reject it with the path witness if it omits internal-label information. Any lower-bound alternative must quantify its representation class, keep every instance Multiway-Cut-feasible, and avoid pairwise-signature inference.
